subject: Cutover verification: degraded-path reconciliation & targeted KV cache priming
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@acme-finance.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: sre-team@acme-finance.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: cutover validation - odd latency spike & 502s on edge

Hi Olga / Connor,

We started seeing intermittent degraded paths immediately after the cutover window closed (between 07:30 - 08:00 PDT). Symptoms: bursty 502s on a subset of requests, sporadic 400-600ms P95 increases, and increased KV cache miss rate in our traces. We collected a pcap and some application traces (attached).

We've isolated it to a small subset of prefixes routed through the new transit fabric — looks like a path flapping event and repeated cold KV misses for a handful of sessions. Can Redwood run a targeted KV priming and confirm any routing reconciliation steps you performed? We need a short-lived mitigation while we decide next steps.

Attachments: network-trace-acme-0602.pcap

Thanks,
Nora Patel
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Finance
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Nora Patel <nora@acme-finance.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: cutover validation - odd latency spike & 502s on edge

Thanks Nora — appreciate the trace. I'm escalating into a targeted checklist so we can both run controlled mitigation steps without a broad rollback. TL;DR: we'll (1) reconcile any ephemeral route state, (2) run a directed KV priming for affected prefixes/sessions, (3) monitor for reappearance over the next 2 hours.

Planned immediate actions (concise):
- Connor: run the KV priming script for prefixes listed in the trace (script attached as step in runbook).
- Mina: validate BGP path stability and clear any stale next-hops on egress gateways.
- I'll coordinate telemetry windows and collect a short kvcache warmup log.

I've attached the trimmed postcutover-smoke-checklist.pdf with the targeted steps we plan to run (Section C: targeted priming + routing reconciliation). Can you confirm you have telemetry sampling for spans 07:20-08:40 PDT (so we can compare before/after)?

Expected impact: priming should reduce cold-miss latency within ~5-10 minutes for primed prefixes; routing reconciliation should eliminate flapping if stale routes are cleared. If this doesn't resolve within 30m we'll open a tactical bridge.

Attachments: postcutover-smoke-checklist.pdf

—
Olga Petrov
Network Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, Nora Patel <nora@acme-finance.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, michael_grant@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: cutover validation - odd latency spike & 502s on edge

On it — kicked off targeted KV priming for the prefix set extracted from the pcap (see run id below). I ran a focused warmup, forced cache loads for the top 20 session keys observed in the trace. Early telemetry: cache-miss rate for those keys dropped from ~18% to 2% within 8 minutes.

Short log (trimmed):
[2027-06-02T09:05:14Z] run-id: rp-0602-priming-42 start
[2027-06-02T09:06:07Z] primed key batch 1 (20 keys)
[2027-06-02T09:12:20Z] priming complete; observed P95 for affected-tenant down from 560ms -> 140ms

I'll attach the full kv warmup log to this thread (kv_warmup_log.txt). I'm also running a BGP neighbor health check now.

run-id: rp-0602-priming-42

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: sre-team@acme-finance.com, Nora Patel <nora@acme-finance.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, michael_grant@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Cutover verification: degraded-path reconciliation & targeted KV cache priming

Team — quick status update after the focused actions:

- KV priming run (rp-0602-priming-42) completed successfully. Attached kv_warmup_log.txt contains timestamps and the key batches.
- BGP reconciliation: Mina cleared two stale next-hop entries on egress-gw-3 that correlated with the flaps; neighbor flaps cleared within 3 minutes of reset.
- Observability: P95 and 502 rates on the previously-affected prefixes have returned to baseline; we saw a sustained reduction in error rate for 55 minutes post-prime.

Short conclusion: the immediate symptoms were mitigated by the targeted priming + clearing stale egress state. No full rollback required. Proposed next steps:
1) Keep elevated sampling for 48 hours and run the full postcutover smoke checklist at T+24h (I scheduled a checkpoint at 2027-06-03 08:00 PDT).
2) Produce a one-pager postmortem if we see reoccurrence within 72 hours.
3) We'll prep a brief runbook addendum capturing the targeted priming command and how to scope prefixes.

If Acme wants the on-call bridge notes or raw traces exported to your secure bucket, tell us and we will push them.

—
Olga Petrov
Network Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Nora Patel <nora@acme-finance.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: sre-team@acme-finance.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cutover verification: degraded-path reconciliation & targeted KV cache priming

Thanks, Olga / Connor — that's great news. We validated the downstream app traces and confirmed error rate is back to baseline. We'll keep the elevated sampling for 48 hours and share anything that looks suspicious.

Please upload the runbook addendum and the kv_warmup_log.txt to the shared Drive link you mentioned and send a pointer when ready. Also — can you include a short note on the exact BGP commands Mina used to reconcile the stale next-hops? Our network team would like the specifics for their postmortem.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

- Nora
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Finance
